advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Give the bare `next(...)` heading lookups in test_rebar_debug_step0.py a default (or wrap in an explicit assert) so a removed heading fails with a clear message rather than StopIteration.
evidence: tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step0.py:42: `step0 = next(n for n, line in enumerate(body.splitlines(), 1) if line.startswith("# Step 0 — Orient"))`
tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step0.py:45: `phase1 = next(n for n, line in enumerate(body.splitlines(), 1) if line.startswith("# Phase 1"))`
tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step0.py:51: `step0 = next(line for line in _skill().splitlines() if line.startswith("# Step 0 — Orient"))`
A missing heading yields `StopIteration` (an error, not a clear assertion message) rather than a diagnosable failure naming which heading is absent.
advisory.finding: test_step_0_precedes_phase_1 and test_step_0_applies_to_the_fast_path_too use bare next(genexpr) with no default, so if the '# Step 0 — Orient' or '# Phase 1' heading is ever renamed/removed the test fails with an opaque StopIteration instead of a descriptive AssertionError.
advisory.suggested_fix: Use `next((...), None)` and assert the result is not None with a message naming the missing heading, mirroring the descriptive _heading_line helper already in the file.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace prose-wording greps (`including closed tickets`, `**Open or in progress**`, `resume the existing`, `regression`) with assertions on canonical, parser-consumed tokens (the actual `rebar`/`git` commands or the dossier-line templates) so the tests survive a behavior-preserving reword.
evidence: test_the_choice_between_link_and_resume_has_a_decision_rule: assert "**Open or in progress**" in body; assert "resume that ticket in place" in body; assert "**Closed, and the behavior is back**" in body; assert "regression" in body

Rule-5 litmus: 'An LLM is NOT a non-human consumer — a prose/heading grep that merely guards the author’s wording IS a change-detector.' These tokens are prose, not commands the agent executes or canonical identifiers a tool parses.
advisory.finding: Several Step 0 tests assert on free-prose wording that only a human/LLM reader consumes (not a parser/CI/validator), so they break on a behavior-preserving reword of the skill without any change to the protocol's behavior — the change-detector antipattern under the Rule-5 litmus.
scenarios: An editor rewords 'including closed tickets' to 'across all statuses including closed' — behavior identical, test goes red.
'resume that ticket in place' reworded to 'continue the existing ticket' — protocol unchanged, test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Pin the structural contract via the runnable commands and dossier-line templates the agent literally emits/executes (e.g. the `--status open,in_progress` flag, the `rebar link <new> <existing> duplicates` command, the `Step 0(a): duplicates <id> (<alias>)` template line) rather than descriptive prose.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the absence check to catch any `--before=` fed a value without the `/ 1000000000` divide (or without the `@` seconds prefix), e.g. assert no `--before=` occurrence lacks the divide, so re-introduced broken spellings are caught.
evidence: The defect the diff exists to prevent is any raw-nanosecond `--before=` form; only two literal spellings are excluded, so a regression using a third spelling passes.
advisory.finding: test_raw_nanosecond_before_form_is_absent forbids only two exact spellings of the broken command (`--before="<created_at>"` and `--before="$created_at"`), leaving the most likely regression re-introductions uncovered — e.g. an unquoted `--before=<created_at>`, `--before="${created_at}"`, or a raw 19-digit literal `--before="1787354756915214001"`.
scenarios: An edit re-introduces the bug as `--before="${created_at}"` or `--before=1787354756915214001`; both absence assertions still pass because they match neither literal, so the regression ships green.
